{{Distinguish|Overlapping interval topology}}
In mathematics, and especially [[general topology]], the '''interlocking interval topology''' is an example of a [[topology]] on the set {{nowrap|1=''S'' := '''R'''<sup>+</sup> \ '''Z'''<sup>+</sup>}}, i.e. the set of all positive [[real number]]s that are not positive [[Natural number|whole numbers]].<ref name=SS7778>Steen & Seebach (1978) pp.77 – 78</ref>

== Construction ==

The open sets in this topology are taken to be the whole set ''S'', the empty set ∅, and the sets generated by

:<math> X_n := \left(0,\frac{1}{n}\right) \cup (n,n+1) = \left\{ x \in {\mathbf R}^+ : 0 < x < \frac{1}{n} \ \text{ or } \ n < x < n+1 \right\}. </math>

The sets generated by ''X<sub>n</sub>'' will be formed by all possible unions of finite intersections of the ''X<sub>n</sub>''.<ref name=SS4>Steen & Seebach (1978) p.4</ref>
